key_insight: RFM-AGOP efficiently extracts multi-dimensional refusal subspaces in LLMs, replacing slower subspace methods with a fast, probe-informed recursive approach.
engineering_relevance: This makes safety steering and interpretability workflows more scalable, especially for long-chain reasoning models where existing extraction methods are too expensive to run repeatedly.
method: Adapt the Recursive Feature Machine (RFM) algorithm for subspace discovery.
Initialize RFM with a probe-informed starting point to target refusal-related activations.
Use the resulting subspace to identify and ablate refusal behavior in both reasoning and non-reasoning models.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the method identifies refusal subspaces in seconds on Qwen 3 and Qwen 2.5, and outperforms alternative methods on the ablation task.
watch_item: The abstract notes that the relationship between subspaces found by different methods is still not well understood, so equivalence and robustness remain open questions.
paper_title: Fast Multi-dimensional Refusal Subspaces via RFM-AGOP
